questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To be honest, it was random, but I had in mind that I wanted to choose a country that I normally would not travel to. However, I really chose it well as nature is insanely beautiful and I was shocked that this was in Europe. You can both swim in lakes and go skiing during the exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Bern sends you everything you will need to know. They have a thorough introduction programme, where you can join a zoom call and ask questions. They send you information from accommodation possibilities to vintage bicycle shops.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The introduction week at the campus was fun and good. They give a lot of information about everything and you have the possibility to meet all the other exchange students, which in my case was a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found a student lodge, which is quite popular for exchange students. My host university also had this recommended. I chose a Studentlodgde Bumpliz Nord, which helped a lot with my social life and meeting friends. Some of my fellow exchange students chose other student lodges (Wankdorf) or private accommodations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
If you want to have the possibility to meet a lot of other students, then I would recommend a student lodge. However, if you would like to live in private accommodation you also have the possibility to meet other students during the introduction week.

The prices at the student lodge were expensive, but worth it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: KSL and ILLIAS were quite difficult to understand in the beginning, but during introduction week they give you an information sheet on how to register for different courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could ask by email, zoom call (intro) or use the given information sheet about registering.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered quite earlier than everyone else just to be sure, but I got in every class. The good thing was that a lot of my fellow exchange students and swiss students could pick and choose what class to attend during the first few of the semester. They changed courses just by writing an email to the professor, so there is a lot of flexibility here.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I checked the exam dates and the attendance date, which were so important. I made a weekly schedule and made sure that I had time during the exams to study, because the academic level is quite high, so you need to study and attend in order to pass.
And I specifically choose not to have a writing/sit-in exam - only projects or presentations!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of my courses was quite high. Higher than the level of courses I have taken at my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses I took didn't have a lot of students attending. In one of my courses, we were only four, so the professor will expect you to work hard. I didn't attend all my classes, because of overlap and because I sometimes wanted to hike/have fun instead. But I took my assignments seriously and worked effectively when needed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Empirical Macroeconomics II
2. Quantitative Macroeconomics 
3. Spatial Methods using Python for Economists 
4. Environmental Econometrics
5. Labour Economics
6. Banking Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
These are the ones I will recommend if you are planning on not dying during the semester:
Spatial Methods using Python for Economists (group project),  Environmental Econometrics (only assignments), and Banking theory (one nice midterm and group exam). 
Don't take quantitive macroeconomics if you are not good in loops and more advanced stuff (Value function iteration) in Matlab (this one killed me every week, and also all the other students). Even though I received the best grade in Empirical Macro II I would not recommend it if you are not planning on working hard (and everything is mostly in coding, and Matlab), but the professor is nice and helpful (Luca Benati). I didn't know Matlab before attending, but I think it is something you can learn fast if you have some experience in coding.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You should expect Switzerland to be expensive. However, if you do your research on half-fare cards and stuff like that transportation will get so much cheaper. The prices above are the maximum that I would use, so you can either use less or more. But I spend most of my money on train tickets for hiking and going around Switzerland, which I really recommend because it is so beautiful!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to a bar and eating out is more expensive than what I'm used to in CPH. A pizza or durum is above 120 kr., which was insane.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Important: The university of Bern offers so many different sports clubs and opportunities (soccer, mountain biking, paragliding, boxing, dancing etc.) and two free gyms close to the university. The free gym possibility was so nice for me and my friends as otherwise, it would have been so expensive. 

An organisation for exchange students called ESN arranged so many different trips for only 15 CHF including train transportation. They really did a good job and they also gave us the possibility to party and go on a skiing trip with all the exchange students. 

The clubs were not that great in Bern, but still fun. The bars are nice and cosy.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Hiking, seeing different cities (Zurich is also fun for eating out and clubbing). 

My friends and I really enjoyed hiking and swimming in the Aare river in Bern during summer. Or drinking a beer near the parliament.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel around Switzerland. The mountains are insanely beautiful. Visit french and Italian-speaking places also e.g., Valais, Mont Blanc or Lugano. 

Don't just spend time in one place. Try to see everything.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. They speak German and are alike us Danes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just ask questions and be nice. They are really welcoming and a lot of the students there are international or from other places in Switzerland.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging. Maybe the fondue which is so good, but I'm lactose intolerant. Some other exchange students found swiss people to be cold, but I think it is the same way of life for Danish people. So they were really easy to interact with for me.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their hiking culture and drinking a beer at the top of a mountain.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Check exam dates, and bring hiking shoes/ a good jacket and money.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be shy (interact with people), don't stress (everything will be alright) and enjoy every single moment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The mountains, friends and passing all my courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses were difficult.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I did not think I would enjoy this exchange so much. I fell in love with Switzerland and the mountains. To be honest, I have seen a lot of different nature in the world, but nothing compares to Switzerland, because there are always transportation and hiking possibilities. No matter what hike we chose it was always incredibly beautiful.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
